answer: Mechanism: drift-bound cipher streams. The coordinator assigns each agent a rotating onyx cipher key and a secret schedule of micro-delays; agents must return tokens at those delays, encrypting local clock-jitter residuals into the stream. A duplicated runtime shares jitter correlations and cipher nonce patterns, so cross-correlating token streams makes clones self-revealing. Attacker cost: independent entropy hardware and per-clone timing calibration, plus continuous jitter maintenance. Agents may wander across delay slots, but residuals bind each stream to one runtime.
